title: Praying to Saints in the same forms used to God is treason against the divine majesty
source_text: XXIX. Denique non existimant illos effugere crimen laesae majestatis divinae, qui in suis precibus iisdem formulis Sanctos compellant atque Deum, poscentes ab iis gratiam & gloriam, ac bona quaelibet corporis & animae: licet non habeant Sanctos pro primis bonorum illorum authoribus, sed solum tanquam eorum sub Deo largitores & administratores: sicuti crimen illud non effugeret, qui sub praetextu simili Sanctis immolare vellet.
pass_a_gloss: Finally they do not think that those escape the crime of injured divine majesty who in their prayers address the Saints with the same formulas as God, asking from them grace and glory and any goods of body and soul: although they do not take the Saints for the first authors of those goods, but only as their givers and administrators under God: just as one would not escape that crime who under a similar pretext wished to immolate to the Saints.
pass_b_english: Using toward the Saints the same prayer-forms used toward God, and asking them for grace, glory, and any bodily or spiritual good, is treated as an offense against God's majesty.
It does not help to call the Saints not the first authors but only givers and stewards under God.
The same pretext would not excuse sacrificing to them.

choices.why: The offense is the form of absolute prayer, not the mere mention of a Saint.
rejected: a difference of mental reservation that clears the words
